yzoh9l:204: Progress state is written to two sets of carriers simultaneously—a highly scannable terminal summary for humans (numbers, ratios, anomalies) and a structured state file for Agent reading (task ID, status, artifact path, failure reason). The deep logic of this design: humans need the intuitive sense of "how far have we gotten" when recovering; Agent needs precise instructions on "where to continue from", and the two data structures are completely heterogeneous. Forcibly merging them not only creates redundancy but also increases parsing noise for the Agent. Many teams implement persistence but overlook the dual-channel design, which is a common hidden cause of long-running task recovery failure.
